questions.enonce_markdown: A sole proprietorship is considered as a one man business because:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A sole proprietorship is a business owned, financed and usually managed by one person. Because he is the only owner and has few or no partners, he does most of the work himself (buying, selling, bookkeeping), perhaps with the help of a few employees or family members. It is therefore called a one man business.

Owning many types of businesses (A) is not what defines it, specialization (B) is a weakness of a sole trader (he has to do many jobs), and quality of service (D) is not linked to the number of owners.

**Answer: C.**

choix.texte: He owns many types of businesses alone
He enjoys all the advantages of specialization
He does most of the work alone
He offers quality services to the customers

questions.enonce_markdown: A market where the commodity sold is homogeneous and firms are price-takers, is called:
questions.corrige_markdown:
In a perfect market (perfect competition) the goods are homogeneous (identical), there are very many buyers and sellers, each firm is too small to influence the price and so is a price-taker, and buyers and sellers have full knowledge of the market. Monopoly, oligopoly and imperfect markets have fewer firms or differentiated products and firms that can influence the price.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
This question is based on the table below which shows the output of a farmer as he employs different numbers of workers:

| Number of workers | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Total product (kg) | 7 | 15 | 24 | 36 | 50 | 54 |

At what level of output is average product highest?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Average product (AP) = total product / number of workers.

| Workers | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Total product (kg) | 7 | 15 | 24 | 36 | 50 | 54 |
| AP (kg) | 7 | 7.5 | 8 | 9 | 10 | 9 |

The highest average product is 10 kg per worker, reached with 5 workers, when the total product is 50 kg. The question asks for the LEVEL OF OUTPUT (total product), not for the value of the average product itself (10 kg), so the answer is 50 kg. The trap is to choose the largest total product (54 kg), which gives a lower average (9 kg).

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: An industry that locates near the source of raw materials can be considered as a:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Industries whose raw materials lose a lot of weight during processing (for example sawmills, cocoa or palm-oil mills, sugar and ore processing) locate near the source of raw materials, because it is cheaper to process them where they are found and transport the lighter finished product. These are called weight-losing (bulk-reducing) industries. A footloose industry can locate anywhere, industrial inertia is the tendency of an industry to stay where it started even when the original advantages have gone, and a weight-gaining industry locates near its market.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The problem of perishability was solved by which function of money?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Under barter, goods such as fish, tomatoes or plantains go bad (perishable), so wealth could not be kept for later. Money does not perish, so a seller can keep the value of his goods in the form of money and spend it later. This is the function of money as a store of value. The medium of exchange function solves the problem of double coincidence of wants, the measure of value solves the problem of valuing goods, and the standard of deferred payment allows debts to be settled in the future.

**Answer: B.**

choix.texte: Money as a medium of exchange
Money as a store of value
Money as a measure of value
Money as a standard of deferred payment

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following factors of production is highly affected by the law of diminishing returns?
questions.corrige_markdown:
The law of diminishing returns states that when more and more units of a variable factor are added to a fixed factor, the extra output obtained from each additional unit eventually falls. Land is the classic fixed factor: its size cannot be increased in the short run, so adding more workers, fertilizer or seeds to the same plot of land gives smaller and smaller extra output. The factor of production most affected by the law is therefore land.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: What is the per capita income of a country with a population of 5 million people and a national income 200 million FCFA?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Per capita income = national income / population = 200,000,000 FCFA / 5,000,000 people = 40 FCFA per person. The other options come from multiplying the two numbers or from slips in the number of zeros.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: An upward movement along the same demand curve is called:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A movement along the same demand curve is caused only by a change in the price of the good itself. Moving UP the curve means the price has risen, so the quantity demanded falls: this is a contraction in demand (a movement down the curve, with a fall in price, is an extension). A fall or an increase in demand (A and B) means a SHIFT of the whole curve, caused by other factors such as income or tastes.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: When the revenue from the tax is greater than the cost of collecting the tax, this explains the principle of:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Adam Smith's canons of taxation include: equity (fairness), certainty (the taxpayer knows what, when and how much to pay), convenience (the tax is paid in a manner and at a time convenient to the taxpayer) and economy (the cost of collecting the tax must be small compared with the revenue it yields). A tax whose yield is greater than its collection cost respects the principle of economy.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following is an example of an unincorporated business unit:
questions.corrige_markdown:
An unincorporated business has no separate legal personality: the owners and the business are legally the same, so the owners are personally liable for its debts. Sole proprietorships and partnerships are unincorporated. Private and public limited companies are incorporated (registered as separate legal persons), and co-operative societies are also registered bodies with a legal personality of their own.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The most effective way of achieving equitable distribution of income and wealth in an economy is by:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A progressive tax takes a larger percentage of income from richer people than from poorer people. The government can then use the revenue for the poor (health, education, social transfers), which reduces inequality. Indirect taxes (A) tend to be regressive because they take a larger share of the income of the poor, agricultural shows (C) only promote farming, and increasing the money supply (D) causes inflation, which hurts people on low fixed incomes.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
The coefficient of elasticity of demand in the diagram below is:

![fig-1](gce-ol-economics-2025-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_1.png)
questions.corrige_markdown:
The demand curve D is a vertical straight line at quantity Q. Whatever the price, the quantity demanded stays at Q, so the percentage change in quantity demanded is zero. Price elasticity of demand = % change in quantity demanded / % change in price = 0 / (% change in price) = 0. Demand is perfectly inelastic. A horizontal demand curve would give an elasticity of infinity (B), which is the usual trap.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A country where the labour force cannot fully exploit its resources is said to be:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A country is under populated when its population is smaller than the optimum population: there are not enough workers to use the natural resources fully, so output per head is below what it could be. Over population is the opposite case (too many people for the resources). Sparsely populated (C) describes a low population DENSITY, not the relation between labour and resources, and option D is not a description of a country.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Labour cannot be acquired and owned like the other factors of production because:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A firm can buy and own land and capital goods, but it cannot buy and own workers (this would be slavery). It can only hire the services of workers for an agreed time and wage, and the worker remains a free person. This makes labour different from the other factors. Mobility, skill levels and scarcity do not explain why labour cannot be owned.

**Answer: A.**

choix.texte: Labour is the most mobile factor of production
Labour can be both skilled and unskilled

questions.enonce_markdown: What is the meaning of BEAC?
questions.corrige_markdown:
BEAC is the French abbreviation of Banque des Etats de l'Afrique Centrale, that is the Bank of Central African States. It is the common central bank of the CEMAC countries (Cameroon, Chad, Central African Republic, Congo, Gabon and Equatorial Guinea) and issues the common currency, the CFA franc (FCFA).

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Mr. A earns 350,000FCFA as income and pays a tax of 5%. If the rate is increased to 15%, how much extra tax does he pay?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Tax at 5%: 350,000 x 5/100 = 17,500 FCFA.
Tax at 15%: 350,000 x 15/100 = 52,500 FCFA.
Extra tax = 52,500 - 17,500 = 35,000 FCFA (or directly 10% of 350,000 = 35,000 FCFA).

The trap is option C (52,500 FCFA), which is the TOTAL tax at the new rate, not the extra amount.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: In a partnership, a nominal partner is one who:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A nominal partner lends only his name to the firm (usually a well-known person who gives the business prestige and credit). He contributes no capital, does not take part in management and does not share in the profits, although he remains liable to outsiders. Option A describes an active partner, B a sleeping (dormant) partner, and C describes the position of an ordinary partner.

**Answer: D.**

choix.texte: Contributes capital and takes part in management
Contributes capital and does not take part in management
Shares in the profits and losses of the business
Allows only his name to be used in the business

questions.enonce_markdown: A commercial bank has a deposit of 500,000FCFA and a cash ratio of 10%. How much deposit can the bank create?
questions.corrige_markdown:
The credit (deposit) multiplier is 1 / cash ratio = 1 / 0.10 = 10. The total deposits the banking system can support from an initial cash deposit of 500,000 FCFA are 500,000 x 10 = 5,000,000 FCFA = 5 million FCFA (equivalently 500,000 / 0.10). Option A comes from using a cash ratio of 0.5% by mistake, and D is just the initial deposit.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Identify the fixed costs from the combinations below:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Fixed costs do not change with the level of output in the short run. Rents and depreciation (the loss in value of machines and buildings with time) are both fixed costs. Wages (in A and C) and raw materials (C) change with output and are variable costs. In D, machines are an asset (capital goods), not a cost item, so the only combination made entirely of fixed costs is B.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Trade between Cameroon and France can be described as:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Bilateral trade is trade between TWO countries, here Cameroon and France. Multilateral trade involves three or more countries. Foreign trade and external trade are general names for any trade between a country and the rest of the world, so they do not say how many countries are involved.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: An increase in the supply of maize in the market with a constant demand, will lead to:
questions.corrige_markdown:
When supply increases and demand is constant, the supply curve shifts to the right. At the old price there is a surplus of maize, so sellers lower the price until the market clears at a new equilibrium with a lower price and a larger quantity. Demand itself does not fall (C): the quantity demanded rises along the demand curve (an extension in demand).

**Answer: B.**

choix.texte: Increase in the price of maize
Fall in the price of maize
Fall in the demand for maize
No change in the price of maize

questions.enonce_markdown: The low level of industrialization in Cameroon is as a result of:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The best answer among the four options is the low level of consumption. The average income of the population is low, so the home market is small and weak: purchasing power is limited, and local industries cannot sell enough to justify large-scale production. Other problems that are often given for the low level of industrialization are inadequate capital, poor infrastructure (roads, electricity) and a limited supply of technical skills. Labour is not scarce in Cameroon (D is false), the quality of goods is not the cause (B), and taxes alone do not explain the situation (C). This question calls for the option closest to the usual textbook answer.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A trade fair involves the exhibition of goods and services of:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A trade fair is an exhibition where producers display their goods and services to attract buyers and make contacts. It is open to both home (local) producers and foreign producers, which makes it a way of promoting trade between countries. A show limited to home producers would be a local or national exhibition.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: An economic system in which prices are determined by the forces of demand and supply is called:
questions.corrige_markdown:
In a market (free enterprise or capitalist) economy, prices are set by the interaction of demand and supply in the market, without government direction. In planned or command economies (A and C) the state decides what to produce and at what prices. A mixed economy combines the market and government intervention.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Token coins are coins:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Token coins (for example 5 FCFA, 10 FCFA or 25 FCFA coins) are made of cheap metal, so the value of the metal they contain (the intrinsic value) is much smaller than the value written on them (the face value). They are accepted because the law makes them legal tender. Full-bodied coins are those whose face value equals their intrinsic value (C).

**Answer: D.**

choix.texte: Which are not backed by gold
Whose face values are equal to the intrinsic value
Whose face values are greater than the intrinsic value

questions.enonce_markdown: What term is used to describe the malpractice of selling goods cheaper in foreign markets than in the home market?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Dumping is the sale of goods in a foreign market at a price lower than in the home market (sometimes below the cost of production), to destroy competition or to get rid of a surplus. Devaluation and depreciation are falls in the value of a currency, and deflation is a fall in the general price level.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The population of a country is structured as follows: 10% aged, 30% working age and 60% young. If the population is 20 million people, determine the dependent population.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The dependent population is made up of the people who do not work and depend on the working population: the young and the aged.
Dependent share = 60% + 10% = 70%.
Dependent population = 70/100 x 20 million = 14 million.

The working population is 30% x 20 million = 6 million (option C, the usual trap), and the young alone are 12 million (option B).

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
The question is based on the diagram below.

![fig-2](gce-ol-economics-2025-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_2.png)

From the diagram, P2 is called?:
questions.corrige_markdown:
On the diagram, demand D and supply S meet at the equilibrium price P1 and quantity Q1. P2 is BELOW the equilibrium price. At P2 the quantity demanded is Q2 and the quantity supplied is only Q3, so there is excess demand (a shortage) of Q3 Q2. A price fixed by the government below the equilibrium price, which sellers are not allowed to exceed, is a maximum price (price ceiling), for example a price control on essential foods or rent. A minimum price would be set ABOVE the equilibrium and would create a surplus, and P1 is the equilibrium price.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A situation in national income where the inputs of some firms are the output of other firms will likely lead to:
questions.corrige_markdown:
When the output of one firm (for example flour sold to a baker) is the input of another firm, counting the value of both the intermediate goods and the final goods would count the same value more than once. This error is called double counting. To avoid it, only the value of final goods and services (or the value added at each stage) is included in the national income.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Cost which can be incurred even when production has not started are called:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Fixed costs (such as rent, insurance and interest on loans) must be paid whether the firm produces nothing or a lot, so they are incurred even before production starts. Variable costs (raw materials, wages of casual workers) only appear when production takes place. Average and marginal costs are calculated from production levels, so they do not exist at zero output.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following is a characteristic of under development?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Under-developed countries depend heavily on the primary sector (agriculture, fishing, mining and forestry), which employs most of the population and supplies most of the exports. They have low, not high, per capita income, low resource utilization and a low level of consumption. High reliance on the primary sector is therefore the characteristic.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The charging of different prices for the same product to different consumers with reasons not related to the cost of production is called:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Price discrimination is the practice of a seller charging different prices for the same product to different buyers or in different markets (for example by age, area or time of day) for reasons that are not linked to differences in cost. Price differentials (A) are differences in price that DO reflect differences in cost, such as quality or transport costs.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: In an economy the government expenditures and taxes are good instruments of:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Fiscal policy is the use of government spending and taxation to influence the economy (output, employment, prices). Monetary policy uses the money supply and interest rates and is run by the central bank. Economic policy (D) is a general name that also includes fiscal and monetary policy, so the precise answer is fiscal policy.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A population with a greater number of people in the old age group will likely lead to:
questions.corrige_markdown:
People in the old age group are mostly retired and no longer work, so the share of the population that is in the labour force falls and the supply of labour falls. The dependency burden increases, so output does not rise (C) and government spending on pensions and health care tends to rise, not fall (D).

**Answer: B.**

choix.texte: An increase in the supply of labour
A fall in the supply of labour

questions.enonce_markdown: A bank receives a cash deposit of 100,000FCFA. If the cash ratio is 2.5%, how much cash should the bank hold?
questions.corrige_markdown:
The cash ratio is the percentage of deposits that a bank keeps in cash. Cash to hold = 2.5/100 x 100,000 = 2,500 FCFA. The remaining 97,500 FCFA (option C) can be lent out or invested.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Beef and hides are said to be in:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Joint supply exists when two goods come from the same production process, so a rise in the supply of one automatically raises the supply of the other. A cow slaughtered for meat gives both beef and hides. Joint demand (A) is for goods used together, such as cars and fuel, and competitive supply (C) is for goods that use the same resources, such as maize and groundnuts on the same field.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A merger between a brewery and a cigarette manufacturing company is called:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A conglomerate is formed by the merger of firms producing unrelated goods and services, here beer and cigarettes, which are not at the same stage of the same production chain. Horizontal integration joins firms at the same stage of production of the same product (two breweries) and vertical integration joins firms at different stages of the same product (a brewery and a barley farm).

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The money value of goods and services produced by factors of production within a country is called:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Gross Domestic Product (GDP) is the money value of all final goods and services produced within the geographical borders of a country in a year, by both nationals and foreigners. GNP adds net income from abroad (the output of the country's factors owned abroad minus that of foreign factors in the country), so it is not limited to production within the country.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Opportunity cost is measured in:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Opportunity cost is the cost of the next best alternative that is given up when a choice is made. It is therefore measured in terms of the alternative forgone (for example, 5 bags of maize given up to produce 2 bags of cocoa). It is a real cost and not necessarily a money cost.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The devaluation of a country's currency will lead to:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A devaluation lowers the official value of the home currency. Suppose the FCFA is devalued: foreigners need less foreign money to buy the same quantity of Cameroonian goods, so the price of exports in foreign currency falls and exports tend to increase. At the same time imports become more expensive in FCFA, so they tend to fall. Options B, C and D are the opposite of what happens.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: When the demand for a good falls as income increases, such a good is called:
questions.corrige_markdown:
For a normal good, demand rises when income rises. For an inferior good (such as cheap second-hand clothes or low quality rice), demand falls as consumers' income rises because they switch to better goods. An ostentatious good (a Veblen good) is demanded more as its price rises, and a Giffen good is an inferior good that takes a large share of income and whose demand rises when its price rises.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
This question is based on the table below;

| Units of output | Fixed Costs FCFA | Variable Costs FCFA | TC FCFA | AC FCFA | MC FCFA |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 10,000 | 5,000 | 15,000 | 15,000 | 15,000 |
| 2 | 10,000 | 8,000 | 18,000 | 9,000 | x |
| 3 | 10,000 | 12,500 | 22,500 | 7,500 | 2,500 |

Calculate the value of x
questions.corrige_markdown:
Marginal cost (MC) is the extra cost of producing one more unit: MC = change in total cost / change in output.
For the second unit: x = TC(2) - TC(1) = 18,000 - 15,000 = 3,000 FCFA.
Check with the other columns: TC(2) = 10,000 + 8,000 = 18,000 and AC(2) = 18,000 / 2 = 9,000 (option D is the AC, not the MC).

Note: with the printed totals, the MC of the third unit would be 22,500 - 18,000 = 4,500 FCFA, not the 2,500 FCFA printed in the table; this printed value does not affect the answer to the question.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
This question is based on the table below.

| Items | Amount in millions FCFA |
|---|---|
| Visible exports | 800 |
| Invisible exports | 500 |
| Visible imports | 250 |
| Invisible imports | 750 |

From the above table calculate the balance of trade.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The balance of trade only takes visible items (goods) into account:
Balance of trade = visible exports - visible imports = 800 - 250 = +550 million FCFA, a surplus.

The invisible items (services) are used for the balance on invisibles: 500 - 750 = -250 million FCFA. Adding both gives the current account balance, 550 - 250 = +300 million FCFA, so using all the items in the table is the trap. (Option A is printed with a typing error, "FCFAA".)

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Inflation caused by excess demand over supply is called:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Demand-pull inflation occurs when aggregate demand is greater than the supply of goods and services at the existing prices (too much money chasing too few goods), which pulls prices up. Cost-push inflation (A) comes from rising costs of production, stagflation (C) is inflation with stagnation and unemployment, and an inflationary spiral (D) is the wage-price circle in which prices and wages keep chasing each other.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A factor reward subjected to uncertainty is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Wages, rent and interest are agreed in advance (by contract) and so are certain. Profit, the reward of the entrepreneur, is what is left after all the other factors have been paid; it can be large, small or even negative (a loss), so it is uncertain.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following is a man-made factor of production?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Capital (machines, tools, buildings, factories) is produced by people to be used to produce other goods, so it is a man-made factor of production. Land is a natural gift, labour is the human effort of the population, and the entrepreneur organizes the other factors.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following is a characteristic of plantation agriculture?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Plantation agriculture (for example rubber, oil palm, banana, tea and cocoa plantations) is large-scale farming of a single cash crop on a big area of land, mostly for export, often with hired labour and heavy capital. Growing a single crop is mono cropping. Mixed cropping, mixed farming and crop rotation are typical of small peasant farms.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following will occur when the Government imposes a quota on imports?
questions.corrige_markdown:
A quota is a physical limit on the quantity of a good that may be imported. Since fewer goods can enter the country, the volume of trade is reduced. Unlike a tariff, a quota does not bring tax revenue to the government (B is false), and it does not directly raise exports (A). Dumping (D) is a practice of exporters, not a result of a quota imposed by the importing country.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: What is the median of the following set of values; 2,8,11,13,15,16,9,20 and 8?
questions.corrige_markdown:
The median is the middle value when the values are arranged in order. Arranged in ascending order, the 9 values are: 2, 8, 8, 9, 11, 13, 15, 16, 20. With 9 values the median is the (9 + 1) / 2 = 5th value, which is 11.

The value 11.3 (option B) is the arithmetic MEAN: (2 + 8 + 8 + 9 + 11 + 13 + 15 + 16 + 20) / 9 = 102 / 9 = 11.33, which is the trap. The mode would be 8 (option A).

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A shift of the production possibility curve to the right implies:
questions.corrige_markdown:
An outward (rightward) shift of the production possibility curve means that the economy's capacity to produce has increased, because of more resources or better technology. This is economic growth (potential growth). Actual growth (C) is a movement from a point inside the curve towards the curve, and economic development (A) is wider than growth because it includes improvements in living standards, health and education.

**Answer: D.**
